answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging an identity price that only honest throughput can repay. Each newcomer stakes a bond, and reputation accrues only through attested work: a wharf receipt, a falcon sighting logged twice, a trellis built. To fake a thousand agents, an attacker must fund a thousand bonds and manufacture a thousand real interactions, so the cost scales linearly while honest peers pay once. Sybils stop being free and become a losing trade.
